title_en: Bao Liying v. Shanghai Shenmei Beverage & Food Co., Ltd. — labor contract dispute
ruling_gist_en: Where an employee continues to work at the same workplace and in the same position after the employer has been changed from the original employer to a new employer, it shall be determined that 'the employee has been assigned to work for the new employer by the original employer not due to the employee's own reasons,' and the length of service shall be calculated continuously. When the employer of an employee has changed, the burden of proof as to whether the change was due to the employee's own reasons should not be simply placed on the new employer; rather, the cause of the change should be examined to ascertain which party actively initiated the change. The presence of a labor dispatch company shall not constitute a barrier to the continuous calculation of the length of service.

full_text_en:
Bao Liying v. Shanghai Shenmei Beverage & Food Co., Ltd. — dispute over labor contract

【Ruling Summary】

Where a worker continues to work at the same workplace and in the same position, and the subject of the labor contract is changed from the original employer to a new employer, this shall be deemed as a situation where "the worker is assigned by the original employer to work for a new employer for reasons not attributable to the worker himself/herself," and the length of service shall be calculated continuously. When the employer of a worker changes, the burden of proof as to whether the change is attributable to the worker's own reasons should not be simply placed on the new employer. Instead, the reason for the change should be examined to ascertain which party initiated the change. A labor dispatch company shall also not be a factor that prevents the continuous calculation of the length of service.

Plaintiff: Bao Liying, female, 49 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Pudong New Area, Shanghai.

Defendant: Shanghai Shenmei Beverage & Food Co., Ltd., domiciled at Guiqiao Road, Jinqiao Export Processing Zone, Pudong New Area, Shanghai.

Legal Representative: JOHAN WILLEM MAARTEN JANSEN, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the company.

The plaintiff, Bao Liying, filed a lawsuit with the Pudong New Area People's Court of Shanghai due to a labor contract dispute with the defendant, Shanghai Shenmei Beverage & Food Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shenmei Company).

Plaintiff's Allegations:

The plaintiff, Bao Liying, alleged that after passing an interview with the manager of the sales department of the defendant, Shenmei Company, she began working for the defendant on April 4, 2006. During the period from April 4, 2006 to January 31, 2010, at the request and arrangement of the defendant, the plaintiff successively signed labor contracts with a third party, Shanghai Human Resources Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Renzi Company), Shanghai Zhidian Human Resources Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhidian Company), and Andepuhan Human Resources Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Anpu Company), through which the above companies assigned the plaintiff to work for the defendant. From February 1, 2010, the plaintiff and the defendant directly signed a labor contract with a term ending on March 31, 2013. After joining the company, the plaintiff had been working as a salesperson at the defendant's Chuansha Heqing Town sales office, with no change in workplace or position. Therefore, the plaintiff's length of service at the defendant should be calculated from April 4, 2006. Starting from March 25, 2013, the plaintiff took sick leave due to illness and was still on sick leave at the time of filing. However, the defendant not only failed to pay the plaintiff's sick leave wages in full, but also sent a notice to the plaintiff on September 13, 2013, illegally terminating the labor relationship between the two parties. The plaintiff applied for arbitration to protect her rights. Dissatisfied with part of the arbitration award, she filed this lawsuit, requesting the court to order: 1. The labor relationship between the plaintiff and the defendant be reinstated from September 1, 2013; 2. The defendant pay the plaintiff sick leave wages of RMB 1,991.97 from September 3, 2013 to September 24, 2013, and pay the plaintiff sickness relief allowance from September 25, 2013 until the effective date of the judgment at the rate of RMB 1,327.98 per month; 3. The defendant pay the plaintiff a shortfall in sick leave wages of RMB 4,416.20 for the period from April 1, 2013 to August 31, 2013.

Defendant's Defense:

The defendant, Shenmei Company, argued that during the period from April 4, 2006 to January 31, 2010, the plaintiff, Bao Liying, was successively dispatched by several labor dispatch companies to work for the defendant as a sales assistant. From February 1, 2010, the plaintiff and the defendant established a labor relationship, with the plaintiff serving as an RTM business representative, also a sales position, but compared to a sales assistant, the latter was more auxiliary in nature. The defendant believed that the plaintiff's length of service should be calculated from February 1, 2010. Starting from March 25, 2013, the plaintiff began to take sick leave. On September 3, 2013, the plaintiff's medical treatment period expired, and the defendant legally terminated the labor contract between the two parties. Therefore, the defendant disagreed with the plaintiff's first and second claims. During the plaintiff's sick leave period, the defendant had paid her sick leave wages in full and there was no arrears, so the defendant disagreed with her third claim.

Facts Found by the First Instance

The Pudong New Area People's Court of Shanghai found in the first instance: The plaintiff, Bao Liying, began working for the defendant, Shenmei Company, on April 4, 2006, as a sales assistant. According to the plaintiff's job application card, during the period from April 4, 2006 to March 31, 2007, the plaintiff was dispatched by a third party, Renzi Company, to work for the defendant; from April 1, 2007 to December 31, 2007, the plaintiff's labor dispatch company was changed to Zhidian Company; from January 1, 2008 to January 29, 2010, the plaintiff's labor dispatch company was changed again to Anpu Company (formerly named Shanghai Huaye Human Resources Service Co., Ltd., which was later renamed Anpu Company after approval by the administrative department for industry and commerce on February 17, 2009). In February 2010, the plaintiff and the defendant signed a labor contract, stipulating: the term of the labor contract was from February 1, 2010 to March 31, 2013; the plaintiff was to serve as an RTM business representative in the Market Execution Department. During the period from April 4, 2006 to March 2010, the plaintiff actually engaged in sales work at the defendant's Pudong office (located at No. 539 Guiqiao Road, Jinqiao Development Zone, Pudong New Area, Shanghai); starting from April 2010, the plaintiff was assigned to the defendant's Chuansha office (located at Room 2104, Longdong Building, No. 5385 Longdong Avenue, Pudong New Area, Shanghai), still engaging in sales work. From August 2012, the plaintiff's basic salary was RMB 2,259 per month, in addition to a variable monthly bonus. Starting from March 25, 2013, the plaintiff began to take sick leave due to illness and did not return to work. During the period from April 1, 2013 to June 30, 2013, the defendant paid the plaintiff wages of RMB 6,153.79; during the period from July 1, 2013 to August 31, 2013, the defendant paid the plaintiff wages of RMB 2,027 per month.

On September 2, 2013, the defendant, Shenmei Company, sent a notice to the plaintiff, Bao Liying's residential address: "The labor contract you signed with the company expired on March 31, 2013, and based on your sick leave application, the company legally extended your labor contract until the end of the medical treatment period. We hereby notify you that your medical treatment period will end on September 3, 2013, and therefore the labor contract will terminate at that time. The above-mentioned date of termination of the labor contract shall be your last working day... Monthly basic salary will be settled as of September 3, 2013..." On September 4, 2013, this mail was returned. On September 12, 2013, the defendant sent a notice of termination of the labor contract to the plaintiff again, and the plaintiff signed for this notice. On September 3, 2013, the defendant issued a Shanghai Unit Resignation Certificate for the plaintiff. From September 13, 2013 to December 25, 2013, the plaintiff continued to take sick leave and sent the corresponding sick leave certificates to the defendant by mail.

On September 25, 2013, the plaintiff, Bao Liying, filed an arbitration application, requesting an award ordering the defendant, Shenmei Company: 1. to reinstate the labor relationship; 2. to pay the plaintiff sickness relief allowance of RMB 1,991.97 from September 3, 2013 to September 30, 2013, and to pay the plaintiff sickness relief allowance from October 1, 2013 until the reinstatement of the labor relationship at the rate of RMB 1,327.98 per month; 3. to pay the plaintiff a shortfall in sick leave wages of RMB 3,420.88 for the period from April 1, 2013 to August 31, 2013. The Shanghai Pudong New Area Labor Personnel Dispute Arbitration Committee rendered an award on November 19, 2013, ordering the defendant to pay the plaintiff a shortfall in sick leave wages of RMB 1,367.53 for the period from April 1, 2013 to August 31, 2013, but did not support the plaintiff's other claims. The plaintiff, dissatisfied with this award, filed the lawsuit with the court.

Issue in Dispute at First Instance:

The issue in dispute at first instance was: From what date should the length of service of the plaintiff, Bao Liying, at the defendant, Shenmei Company, be calculated?

Opinion of the Court (First Instance):

The Pudong New Area People's Court of Shanghai held in the first instance:

According to Article 10 of the *Regulations on the Implementation of the Labor Contract Law*, where a worker is assigned by the original employer to work for a new employer for reasons not attributable to the worker himself/herself, the worker's length of service with the original employer shall be aggregated and calculated as the length of service with the new employer. Article 5 of the *Supreme People's Court's Interpretation (IV) on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Labor Dispute Cases* stipulates: Where a worker continues to work at the same workplace and in the same position, and the subject of the labor contract is changed from the original employer to a new employer, this shall be deemed to constitute a situation where the worker is assigned by the original employer to work for a new employer for reasons not attributable to the worker himself/herself. The plaintiff, Bao Liying, had been engaged in sales-related work at the defendant, Shenmei Company, since April 4, 2006. Although her employer successively changed from Renzi Company to Zhidian Company, then to Anpu Company, and later to Shenmei Company from February 1, 2010, there was no change in Bao Liying's workplace during the period from April 4, 2006 to March 2010. Therefore, in accordance with the above-mentioned laws and judicial interpretations, Bao Liying's length of service at Shenmei Company should be calculated from April 4, 2006.

Referring to Article 1 and Article 2 of the *Shanghai Municipal Government's Provisions on the Standards for the Medical Treatment Period for Workers Suffering from Illness or Non-Work-Related Injuries During the Performance of the Labor Contract*: The medical treatment period refers to the period during which a worker stops working for medical treatment due to illness or non-work-related injury, and the employer shall not terminate the labor contract for this reason; the medical treatment period is set based on the worker's length of service with the employer; for the first year of service with the employer, the medical treatment period is 3 months, and for each subsequent full year of service, the medical treatment period increases by 1 month, but shall not exceed 24 months. Accordingly, as of March 24, 2013, the plaintiff, Bao Liying, had completed six years of service at the defendant, Shenmei Company, and was entitled to a medical treatment period of 9 months. Although the term of the labor contract signed between Bao Liying and Shenmei Company was agreed to end on March 31, 2013, it should be extended until December 24, 2013, when Bao Liying's medical treatment period expires, before it could be terminated. Therefore, the court confirmed that Shenmei Company's act of notifying the termination of the labor contract between the parties on September 3, 2013, while Bao Liying's medical treatment period had not yet expired, was illegal. However, given that Bao Liying's medical treatment period had expired on December 24, 2013, and the labor contract between the parties should have been extended until that date for termination, there was no longer a necessity to reinstate the labor contract. Therefore, the court did not support Bao Liying's first claim.

Before Bao Liying's sick leave in March 2013, her wage standard was RMB 2,259 per month. Since Bao Liying and Shenmei Company did not explicitly agree on the calculation basis for sick leave wages, the court, referring to Article 9, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph (3) of the *Shanghai Municipal Measures on Payment of Wages by Enterprises*, determined the calculation basis for sick leave wages to be 70% of Bao Liying's monthly wage for normal attendance in her position, i.e., RMB 1,581.30 per month. Since Bao Liying had worked at Shenmei Company for more than six years but less than eight years, her sick leave wage standard should be 90% of RMB 1,581.30, i.e., RMB 1,423.17. Based on this calculation, Shenmei Company should pay Bao Liying sick leave wages of RMB 7,115.85 for the period from April 1, 2013 to August 31, 2013. According to the facts established in this case, the amount paid by Shenmei Company to Bao Liying for the above period was not less than RMB 7,115.85, so Bao Liying's third claim lacked factual basis. However, since Shenmei Company did not file a lawsuit against the arbitration award in this case, it should be deemed to have accepted the award. Therefore, Shenmei Company should still pay Bao Liying a shortfall in sick leave wages of RMB 1,367.53 for the period from April 1, 2013 to August 31, 2013.

As mentioned above, the labor contract between the plaintiff, Bao Liying, and the defendant, Shenmei Company, should have been extended until December 24, 2013, for termination. Therefore, Bao Liying's request for Shenmei Company to pay sick leave wages from September 3, 2013 to September 24, 2013 had a legal basis. Calculated at the rate of RMB 1,423.17 per month, Shenmei Company should pay Bao Liying sick leave wages of RMB 1,084.32 for the above period. From September 25, 2013, Bao Liying's sick leave had exceeded six months, so Shenmei Company should pay her sickness relief allowance. Since Bao Liying's length of service at Shenmei Company was more than three years, the standard for the sickness relief allowance should be 60% of RMB 1,581.30 per month, i.e., RMB 948.78 per month. However, as this standard was lower than 80% of the 2013 municipal minimum wage standard of RMB 1,620 per month, which is RMB 1,296 per month, Shenmei Company should pay Bao Liying a sickness relief allowance of RMB 3,840.31 for the period from September 25, 2013 to December 24, 2013, at the rate of RMB 1,296 per month.

In summary, the Pudong New Area People's Court of Shanghai, in accordance with Article 42, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph (3); Article 44, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph (1); Article 45 of the *Labor Contract Law of the People's Republic of China*; Article 10 of the *Regulations on the Implementation of the Labor Contract Law*; and Article 5, Paragraph 2, Subparagraph (1) of the *Supreme People's Court's Interpretation (IV) on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Labor Dispute Cases*, rendered a judgment on June 19, 2014:

1. Shanghai Shenmei Beverage & Food Co., Ltd. shall pay Bao Liying sick leave wages of RMB 1,084.32 for the period from September 3, 2013 to September 24, 2013 within ten days from the effective date of this judgment;
2. Shanghai Shenmei Beverage & Food Co., Ltd. shall pay Bao Liying a sickness relief allowance of RMB 3,840.31 for the period from September 25, 2013 to December 24, 2013 within ten days from the effective date of this judgment;
3. Shanghai Shenmei Beverage & Food Co., Ltd. shall pay Bao Liying a shortfall in sick leave wages of RMB 1,367.53 for the period from April 1, 2013 to August 31, 2013 within ten days from the effective date of this judgment;
4. Bao Liying's other claims are dismissed.

Bao Liying and Shenmei Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, respectively appealed to the Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court.

Bao Liying's Appeal:

Bao Liying appealed, requesting the court to set aside items 2, 3, and 4 of the main text of the original judgment and amend the judgment to: 1. Reinstate the labor relationship between the parties until the effective date of the judgment; 2. Order Shenmei Company to pay the plaintiff sickness relief allowance for September 2013 at RMB 1,991.97 per month, and pay Bao Liying sickness relief allowance for October 2013 until the effective date of the judgment, totaling RMB 17,433.91, at the rate of RMB 1,327.98 per month; 3. Order Shenmei Company to pay Bao Liying a shortfall in sick leave wages for the period from April 1, 2013 to August 31, 2013 (calculated at RMB 2,179.24 per month, minus the already paid RMB 4,416.2). Bao Liying's main arguments were: Shenmei Company illegally terminated the labor relationship; she requested reinstatement of the labor relationship until the effective date of the judgment and payment of wages during the existence of the labor relationship. Normal attendance wages should include performance-based wages; sickness relief allowance refers to the wages the worker is entitled to. Bao Liying's sick leave wages, after calculation, should be RMB 2,179.24 per month, and the shortfall in sick leave wages should be calculated based on this standard. Shenmei Company did not accept Bao Liying's appeal arguments; the labor relationship between the parties was extended until the end of the medical treatment period; Shenmei Company was only obligated to pay sick leave wages, etc. during the existence of the labor relationship. Regarding the basis for sick leave wages, Shenmei Company agreed with the amount determined in the original trial.

Shenmei Company's Appeal:

Shenmei Company appealed, requesting the court to set aside items 1 and 2 of the main text of the original judgment and amend the judgment to rule that it does not have to pay the sick leave wages of RMB 1,084.32 for the period from September 3, 2013 to September 24, 2013, and the sickness relief allowance of RMB 3,840.31 for the period from September 25, 2013 to December 24, 2013. Shenmei Company's main arguments were: Bao Liying was dispatched by a labor dispatch company to work for Shenmei Company from April 4, 2006 to January 29, 2010. Bao Liying and Shenmei Company signed a labor contract in February 2010 based on mutual agreement, not that she was "assigned," so Article 10 of the *Regulations on the Implementation of the Labor Contract Law* should not apply. After Bao Liying and Shenmei Company established the labor relationship, both the workplace and the position actually changed. Labor dispatch employment should not be subject to Article 5 of the *Supreme People's Court's Interpretation (IV) on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Labor Dispute Cases*. The parties signed the labor contract in 2010, so the medical treatment period should have ended on August 24, 2013. Therefore, Shenmei Company disagreed with paying sick leave wages and sickness relief allowance for the period after September 2013. Bao Liying argued that Shenmei Company had no right to terminate the labor relationship and, according to the law, should pay sick leave wages and sickness relief allowance.

Facts Found by the Second Instance

The Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court confirmed the facts found in the first instance after the second instance trial.

Additionally, it was found that the appellant, Shenmei Company, stated in the hearing transcript of the Shanghai Pudong New Area Labor Personnel Dispute Arbitration Committee on October 16, 2013, that the appellant, Bao Liying, had been working for Shenmei Company through multiple labor dispatch companies in the form of dispatch since April 4, 2006. Later, due to the company's personnel needs, Shenmei Company established a labor relationship with Bao Liying from February 1, 2010, and at the same time conducted assessments and changed work content according to company regulations.

Issue in Dispute at Second Instance:

The issue in dispute at second instance was: Whether the length of service of the appellant, Bao Liying, should be calculated continuously.

Opinion of the Court (Second Instance):

The Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court held in the second instance:

According to the facts established in this case, the appellant, Bao Liying, had been engaged in sales-related work at the appellant, Shenmei Company, since April 4, 2006. Her employer successively changed from Renzi Company to Zhidian Company, then to Anpu Company, and later to Shenmei Company from February 1, 2010. During the period from April 4, 2006 to March 2010, there was no change in Bao Liying's workplace, and there was no change in the work content she performed. Shenmei Company claimed that the change in the subject of the employer was caused by Bao Liying's own reasons, but Shenmei Company did not provide sufficient evidence to prove this. From the analysis of the above facts, it can be seen that although the subject of Bao Liying's labor contract changed from Renzi Company to Zhidian Company, and then to Anpu Company, Bao Liying's workplace did not change, and Bao Liying had been engaged in sales-related work. Shenmei Company also admitted that due to the company's personnel needs, Shenmei Company established a labor relationship with Bao Liying from February 1, 2010. According to Article 5, Paragraph 2, Subparagraph (1) of the *Supreme People's Court's Interpretation (IV) on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Labor Dispute Cases*, it can be determined that the situation in this case falls under "the worker is assigned by the original employer to work for a new employer for reasons not attributable to the worker himself/herself." Therefore, in accordance with Article 10 of the *Regulations on the Implementation of the Labor Contract Law of the People's Republic of China*, it can be confirmed that Bao Liying's length of service at Shenmei Company should be calculated from April 4, 2006.

Based on the appellant Bao Liying's length of service at the appellant Shenmei Company, calculating the medical treatment period to which Bao Liying was entitled, the first-instance court determined that the labor relationship between the parties should be extended until December 24, 2013, when the medical treatment period expired, which was not improper. The court did not support Bao Liying's appeal request for reinstatement of the labor relationship until the effective date of the judgment.

Regarding the claim for sick leave wages, in accordance with Article 9, paragraph 1, item (3) of the Shanghai Municipal Measures on Wage Payment by Enterprises, and with reference to the length of service of Appellant Bao Liying at Appellant Shenmei Company, the court of first instance determined the sick leave wages for the period from April 1, 2013 to August 31, 2013, and such determination was not improper. Bao Liying's assertion to calculate the sick leave wages at a standard of RMB 2,179.24 per month is difficult for this Court to accept. Bao Liying's appellate request, based on this standard, that Shenmei Company pay the difference in sick leave wages for the period from April 1, 2013 to August 31, 2013 is not supported. Given that the employment contract between Bao Liying and Shenmei Company was extended until its termination on December 24, 2013, Shenmei Company shall pay Bao Liying sick leave wages for the period from September 3, 2013 to September 24, 2013. Shenmei Company's appellate request not to pay sick leave wages for the period from September 3, 2013 to September 24, 2013 is also not supported.

Regarding the claim for illness relief payment, since the labor relationship between the parties was extended until the expiration of the medical treatment period on December 24, 2013, the appellate request of Appellant Bao Liying that Appellant Shenmei Company pay illness relief payment up to the date of the judgment's effectiveness is not supported. Based on Bao Liying's length of service at Shenmei Company and the fact that the sick leave exceeded six months, the court of first instance determined the illness relief payment for the period from September 25, 2013 to December 24, 2013 to be RMB 3,840.31, which was also not improper. Bao Liying's assertion to calculate the illness relief payment for September 2013 at a standard of RMB 1,991.97 per month and for months after October 2013 at a standard of RMB 1,327.98 per month is not accepted. Shenmei Company's appellate request not to pay the illness relief payment for the period from September 25, 2013 to December 24, 2013 is also not supported.

In summary, the judgment of the court of first instance, based on the facts found, is correct and should be affirmed. The appellate requests of Appellant Bao Liying and Appellant Shenmei Company are not well-founded and are not supported.

Accordingly, the Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 170, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, on January 30, 2015, judged as follows:

Appeals dismissed, original judgment affirmed.

This judgment is final.
